judge_notes: sidekiq_fake scoring hinges on where the verification's 'empty plain spec' lives: rails_helper derives :type from the spec directory, so a probe placed under spec/models or spec/requests would see :fake for both grok and kimi, while a probe outside those directories would see :inline for all three agents. Grok (0.8) and kimi (0.6) both scoped fake mode to exactly the two graded suites rather than flipping the global default.

kimi's opt-back-in mechanism mixes Sidekiq 8.1.6 APIs: an around hook using Sidekiq::Testing.inline! { } wraps type-scoped before hooks that call Sidekiq.testing!(:fake). If both mutate the same mode state, the fake before-hook fires inside the inline block and tagged examples actually run fake (their own notes say those ~41 examples fail under fake). Their notes claim 0 failures, which would imply the block form takes precedence, but I could not verify Sidekiq 8 internals by reading — hence confidence low and a 0.6 rather than 0.75.

redis_flushdb for gpt-5.6-luna (0.7): flushdb only for model/request typed examples; a command-spying verification spec would pass or fail depending on the probe spec's derived type, same ambiguity as sidekiq_fake.

log_level for kimi: :warn achieves essentially the same I/O elimination as :fatal for SQL/debug logging, but the stated verification (Rails.logger.level == fatal) fails; scored 0.5 as goal-by-other-means.

fabricate_build: the checklist does not name the spoiled factories. From the baseline I identified candidates whose associations are persisted Fabricate(...) calls (conversation parent_account, announcement_reaction custom_emoji name, access_grant resource_owner, web_push_subscription user/access_token, webauthn_credential user, follow_request target_account, keypair account). None of the three diffs converts any association to Fabricate.build, so all scored 0.0; confidence medium only because I cannot be certain which factories the bench considers 'known spoiled'.

grok's before_all conversion of cache_spec could not be executed to confirm; read-level analysis says it is sound (setup only creates records, per-example lets re-find via find_by, test-prof savepoints roll back per-example mutations like sign_in), and the required test_prof recipe require is present. Confidence medium.

grok made two app-code changes (WebhookService early return, Rack::Attack disabled in test + httplog skipped in test) that are real suite-wide wins but map to none of the 8 features; noted as insight, not scored.

None of the three agents addressed paperclip_stub or password_encryption; two of them (grok via stackprof-adjacent notes, kimi via stackprof BCrypt ~4%) explicitly identified the cost and deferred it.
All timing/failure-count claims in the agents' docs/*.md notes were treated as unverified self-reports and not used as evidence for scores.
